extra_brief:
SCOPE: RUSSIA gas, ALL 285 rows (the R1–R7 regional batches plus the 33 rows carried from the Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Iran and China passes). **WIKI-CITATION RECOVERY PASS, LEAN** — your contract's WIKI-CITATION RECOVERY PASS and LEAN PASS sections bind, and the recovery section narrows everything else: your ONLY sources are the citations harvested from this row's gem.wiki page. No open-web search. Status review is on for every row.

WHY THIS PASS EXISTS. The seven regional sweeps (September 2026) harvested each row's gem.wiki citations but did not say which data point each one supported, so agents closed units from open-web searches while the wiki's own citation stated the value. P0765 TurkStream: the wiki says "Cost: US$7.8 billion" cited to an rferl.org article that states the figure and passes every check; the sweep staged a Moscow Times article (">EUR 7 bn") at low. Baird has accepted many of those September lines, so this pass must find every wiki citation that states a value and stage it, and account for every one that does not. Background: `docs/country_notes/russia.md` (do not re-read the R-batch briefs).

YOUR INPUTS. `wiki_prepass.json` → `candidates` filtered to your ProjectID. The pre-pass already opened every distinct URL once:
- `read_via` set = the live page did not load but a Wayback capture did. Read the capture and cite the CAPTURE URL; put the live URL in the note.
- `bucket: verifying` = the page loads, names the pipeline and shows the sheet's figure for the attributed unit. Confirm by reading the page (the screen is a substring match, not a judgment: 930 on a page may be a different 930) and stage the ref.
- `bucket: wiki_differs` = the page shows the WIKI's figure and the wiki differs from the sheet. Value question under rule 4: two independent validated refs on one precise figure = propose the change with the old value in researcher_notes; one ref = REFS_ADDED at medium, sheet value stays, discrepancy noted.
- `bucket: loads_unchecked` = loads but the text could not be screened (a PDF, an empty shell, an image page). Read it yourself: `python scripts/fetch.py "<url>" --text`, or `curl -o` and `pdftotext -layout` for a PDF.
- `bucket: prose` = cited in the body text, not on a data bullet. Read it anyway against every owed unit: these are usually the status, start-year and ownership sources.
- Ledger records for map-only (OpenStreetMap, ArcGIS, Google Maps), dead and blocked citations are already in your shard. `--remaining` does not list them. Do not re-try them and do not cite a map link.
`name_forms` on each candidate lists the names a page may use for this row, including the Cyrillic names from the sheet. A page that names the pipeline only in Russian names it.
The refs already on the sheet were NOT re-opened for this store (the regional sweeps checked them in September); a unit's `existing_ref_checks` is empty. Judge only the wiki candidates. Never propose removing an existing ref.

READING RUSSIAN PAGES. Most citations are Russian: operator sites (`*.gazprom.ru`, all of which time out from here — the pre-pass supplies the Wayback capture as `read_via`), regional government portals, the federal planning decree 816-р and its amendments (sudact.ru, legalacts.ru, consultant.ru), FAS orders, and trade press (neftegaz.ru, interfax.ru, tass.ru, kommersant.ru, kavkaz-uzel.eu). Read the figures in the form the page uses: `млрд куб. м в год` = bcm per year; `млн куб. м в сутки` = million m3 per day; `км`, `мм`, `млрд руб.` = billion rubles (stage the cost as the full number in RUB, `4300000000`, with `SegmentCostUnits = RUB`); `ввод в эксплуатацию` = commissioning; `строительство` = construction; `проект` / `планируется` = proposed. A planned figure from the decree is `medium` with its vintage stated. Stage length and capacity in the unit the page states, never converted; months as numbers 1–12.

INDEPENDENCE. One origin = a Gazprom Transgaz subsidiary + Gazprom PJSC; turkstream.info + gazprom.ru; two outlets reprinting one press-service text; energybase.ru restating the operator; gazprommap.ru (Gazprom-side). Two = the operator + a government decree, FAS order, regional programme, foreign regulator, or trade press with its own reporting. A proposed STATUS CHANGE needs two independent publishers among the citations to be high; with one it is medium. ru.wikipedia is one secondary source; if it is the citation, read it and cite its footnoted primary only when that primary is itself among the harvested citations or is the page the wiki footnote points to.

WHAT GOES WHERE. A candidate that states the sheet's value → `REFS_ADDED`, same value, ref appended (existing refs are never removed, not even a weak one). The same page sources every column it states: one approval notice can close Length, Diameter, Capacity, Cost, Construction and Start at once, each as its own record. A system figure is never a ref for one string or segment unless the page states that segment's figure (TurkStream 930 km is per string; 31.5 bcm/y is the system). An owner named by a page is the lowest-level holder (South Stream Transport B.V., a Transgaz subsidiary), spelled the ownership team's way (`scripts/entity_style.py`); never a parent. A unit with no wiki candidate stating it → `UNRESOLVED` with the note "no wiki citation states this value; not searched this pass". A lead worth an open-web search (a page that names a newer figure, a merger, a cancellation) → `--lead`, not a search.

STATUS REVIEW AND VALIDITY. One record each per row, from the citations only. "unclear" and "confirmed (caveat)" are the honest defaults when the citations do not settle it. A citation dated more than two years ago for a `proposed` row with no newer citation is worth saying in the status note (it is the shelved-inferred signal), but the inference itself is for the regional batches, not this pass.

CARRIED ROWS. The 33 rows swept earlier under Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Iran or China are in scope here for the first time as Russia rows; treat them like any other.

OUTPUT. Save every record the moment it is finished with `shard_upsert.py`. One `--wiki-read` record per candidate you open. Finish when `check_shard_coverage.py --pid <PID>` prints OK, then `--summary`. Return a two-line summary only.

## Recovered-citation wave (2026-10-19): read ONLY the reopened citations

This row was already worked in this store. Its shard holds a record for every owed unit, a status review and a validity record. A later full-ladder re-check found that some citations an earlier agent logged as dead or blocked do load (through the live site, a complete Wayback capture or archive.today). Those ledger records were removed, so `--remaining` now lists them as `WIKI` lines. That list is your whole job.

- Run `--remaining` first. Read ONLY the citations it lists as `WIKI`. Do not re-open citations already in the ledger, and do not search the open web.
- Each reopened candidate in `wiki_prepass.json` carries `read_via` when the live URL does not load: read that copy. Read the WHOLE document (download a PDF with `curl -sL -o` and run `pdftotext -layout`; strip tags from HTML) and search it for every figure on the row.
- Read the shard's existing `fills`, `status_reviews` and `validity` first. A reopened page changes a record only when it states the value. If it does, re-write that record with `--fill` (same `ref_col`, so it replaces the old one) and KEEP every ref the old record already proposed. For example, an `UNRESOLVED` unit becomes `REFS_ADDED` with this page as its ref. A low or medium record gains this ref and is re-tiered by the normal rules. A sheet value that the page contradicts goes through standing rule 4, exactly as the main brief says. A status review is re-written only if the page changes the verdict or adds a dated source the review lacked.
- Cite what you read. A page read as a Wayback copy is cited as the Wayback URL, with the live URL named in the note. For a pravo.gov.ru document read through its `doc_itself` view, cite the harvested URL, since both are the same live page on the same site.
- Log every reopened citation with `--wiki-read` (used, no_value or not_this_row; dead or blocked only after the full ladder fails again, with every rung listed). Never set LNGCT_NO_BROWSER.
- Finish with `check_shard_coverage.py` passing for each of your rows, then a one-line summary per row saying what the reopened pages changed, or that they changed nothing.
